title: Fed rate hike announcement on bank stock returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using a market model. The Fed rate hike announcement is a single, well-timed event. We estimate each bank’s normal return using an estimation window (event days −10 to −2) and compute abnormal returns (AR) around the announcement. We then aggregate ARs over the event window [−1, +1] to form CARs and test whether the cross-sectional mean CAR is significantly positive.
- Model: ret_it = alpha_i + beta_i * mkt_ret_t + epsilon_it, with beta_i provided and alpha_i estimated from the estimation window. AR_it = ret_it − (alpha_i_hat + beta_i * mkt_ret_t). CAR_i = sum_{t=-1}^{1} AR_it. We test H0: E[CAR_i] = 0 (or > 0 for one-sided) via a cross-sectional t-test.
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding events for these banks precisely in the [−1, +1] window (event exogeneity).
  - The market model is correctly specified and parameters are stable from the estimation window into the event window.
  - Short-window market efficiency so that the effect is captured within [−1, +1].
  - Cross-sectional inference: CAR_i are independent across firms or any cross-correlation is modest; robustness checks (market-adjusted model, alternative windows, winsorization, placebo window) help assess sensitivity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code to compute CARs around a Fed rate hike announcement
# using a market-model event study with pre-estimated betas and alpha estimated
# from the -10 to -2 estimation window. Includes robustness checks.

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s11_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
required_cols <- c("stock_id", "event_day", "ret", "mkt_ret", "beta")
stopifnot(all(required_cols %in% names(df)))

# 2) Estimation window: days -10 to -2
est <- df[df$event_day >= -10 & df$event_day <= -2, ]

# Estimate alpha_i with fixed beta_i:
# alpha_i_hat = mean( ret_it - beta_i * mkt_ret_t ) over estimation window
est$mm_resid <- est$ret - est$beta * est$mkt_ret
alpha_hat <- aggregate(mm_resid ~ stock_id, data = est, FUN = mean)
names(alpha_hat)[2] <- "alpha_hat"

# 3) Merge alpha_hat back and compute abnormal returns
df2 <- merge(df, alpha_hat, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
if (any(is.na(df2$alpha_hat))) {
  stop("Alpha could not be estimated for some stocks (insufficient estimation window data).")
}

df2$expected_ret <- df2$alpha_hat + df2$beta * df2$mkt_ret
df2$AR <- df2$ret - df2$expected_ret

# Helper function to compute CAR stats for a given AR column and event window
car_stats <- function(data, ar_col = "AR", t_start = -1, t_end = 1, label = "Main") {
  win <- data[data$event_day >= t_start & data$event_day <= t_end, c("stock_id", ar_col)]
  # Sum ARs within the window per stock (CAR_i)
  car_df <- aggregate(win[[ar_col]] ~ stock_id, data = win, FUN = sum)
  names(car_df)[2] <- "CAR"
  N <- nrow(car_df)
  avg <- mean(car_df$CAR)
  sdv <- stats::sd(car_df$CAR)
  se <- sdv / sqrt(N)
  tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, avg / se, NA_real_)
  pval <- if (is.na(tstat)) NA_real_ else 2 * stats::pt(abs(tstat), df = N - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  ci_low <- avg + stats::qt(0.025, df = N - 1) * se
  ci_high <- avg + stats::qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se
  list(label = label, N = N, avg = avg, sd = sdv, se = se, t = tstat, p = pval,
       ci_low = ci_low, ci_high = ci_high, car_df = car_df)
}

# 4) Main result: CAR[-1,+1] using market model
main_res <- car_stats(df2, ar_col = "AR", t_start = -1, t_end = 1, label = "Market model [-1,+1]")

# 5) Robustness checks

# 5a) Market-adjusted model: AR = ret - mkt_ret
df2$AR_MA <- df2$ret - df2$mkt_ret
ma_res <- car_stats(df2, ar_col = "AR_MA", t_start = -1, t_end = 1, label = "Market-adjusted [-1,+1]")

# 5b) Alternative event window: [-2, +2]
alt_res <- car_stats(df2, ar_col = "AR", t_start = -2, t_end = 2, label = "Market model [-2,+2]")

# 5c) Placebo window (pre-event): [-6, -4]
placebo_res <- car_stats(df2, ar_col = "AR", t_start = -6, t_end = -4, label = "Placebo [-6,-4]")

# 5d) Winsorized CARs (1% tails) in main window
winsor <- function(x, p = 0.01) {
  lo <- stats::quantile(x, probs = p, na.rm = TRUE)
  hi <- stats::quantile(x, probs = 1 - p, na.rm = TRUE)
  x[x < lo] <- lo
  x[x > hi] <- hi
  x
}
car_wins <- winsor(main_res$car_df$CAR, p = 0.01)
Nw <- length(car_wins)
avg_w <- mean(car_wins)
sd_w <- stats::sd(car_wins)
se_w <- sd_w / sqrt(Nw)
t_w <- ifelse(se_w > 0, avg_w / se_w, NA_real_)
p_w <- if (is.na(t_w)) NA_real_ else 2 * stats::pt(abs(t_w), df = Nw - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

# 6) Print clear numerical results
cat(sprintf("Main result: Average CAR [-1,+1] (market model) = %.6f (%.3f%%)\n", 
            main_res$avg, 100 * main_res$avg))
cat(sprintf("t = %.3f, p = %.4f, N = %d\n", main_res$t, main_res$p, main_res$N))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f]  ([%.3f%%, %.3f%%])\n\n", 
            main_res$ci_low, main_res$ci_high, 100 * main_res$ci_low, 100 * main_res$ci_high))

cat(sprintf("Robustness - Market-adjusted [-1,+1]: Avg CAR = %.6f (%.3f%%); t=%.3f, p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            ma_res$avg, 100 * ma_res$avg, ma_res$t, ma_res$p, ma_res$N))
cat(sprintf("Robustness - Alternative window [-2,+2]: Avg CAR = %.6f (%.3f%%); t=%.3f, p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            alt_res$avg, 100 * alt_res$avg, alt_res$t, alt_res$p, alt_res$N))
cat(sprintf("Robustness - Placebo window [-6,-4]: Avg CAR = %.6f (%.3f%%); t=%.3f, p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            placebo_res$avg, 100 * placebo_res$avg, placebo_res$t, placebo_res$p, placebo_res$N))
cat(sprintf("Robustness - Winsorized 1%% (main window): Avg CAR = %.6f (%.3f%%); t=%.3f, p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            avg_w, 100 * avg_w, t_w, p_w, Nw))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative or near zero. For an unexpected rate hike, the immediate discount-rate and risk effects typically dominate for equities, including banks, within a very short window. While higher rates can improve bank net interest margins, that tends to materialize over time; the announcement shock often lowers present values and can raise perceived credit risk in the short run.
- Magnitude: Small in absolute terms over [−1, +1], roughly −0.3% to −1.0% average CAR for banks. Robustness checks should yield similar sign; placebo window should be near zero.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model; estimation window [−10,−2]; event window [−1,+1]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank stocks show negative CAR around the rate hike announcement
